title: M2OR-Provenance: a three-task benchmark for olfactory receptor activity prediction
description:
Fixed folds, an evaluation harness, a leakage checker and per-fold uncertainty for three distinct prediction tasks over the M2OR database of olfactory receptor bioassay records:

  • T1 new molecule — scaffold-disjoint, five repeated splits: will this receptor respond to a chemotype not in training?
  • T2 new source — publication-disjoint: will this laboratory's screen report a positive?
  • T3 replication — publication-disjoint, test restricted to pairs already called positive by a training source: will an independent laboratory reproduce a reported positive?

The harness rebuilds pair-level consensus labels inside each fold from training sources only, runs a four-way leakage audit (pairs, molecules, scaffolds, sources) on every fold and reports it as a table, and reports each fold with a percentile bootstrap interval instead of pooling folds into a single figure. Four reference models run on every fold: random forest, L2 logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting on Morgan fingerprints with a receptor indicator, plus a receptor prior that uses no chemical information at all and predicts each receptor's positive rate in the training fold. The prior is a diagnostic, not a recommended model: a result that does not clear it has not been shown to use chemical structure.

Also included: an independent re-implementation of the three headline label-reliability statistics, written without reference to the primary analysis code and using only the Python standard library for parsing; the label-composition and dose-dependence statistics; two controls on the new-source result (a study-design split and a Dawid–Skene relabelling); and the code that regenerates every figure in the accompanying paper.
